SW100-C0529.scope: Exclusive DB/staging/final publication with coherent identity and synced pair; fixed clock, collisions, concurrency and WAL fixtures.
SW100-C0529.rationale: Snapshot identity combines fixed-clock timestamp and UUID; DB and staging files use exclusive no-follow creation, and complete manifest publishes with an exclusive hard link. DB/JSON/directory fsyncs execute before success; colliding foreign empty DB/staging/manifests remain intact. Concurrent and WAL snapshots reopen as coherent hash-matching pairs. SW100-C0337.scope: Exclusive publication of a complete software identity; existing files/symlinks preserved; failures observable.
SW100-C0337.rationale: A fully written, fsynced 0600 temporary seed is linked exclusively to the final name, never truncating an existing identity or seed symlink. Descriptor-relative no-follow loads reject seed/directory symlinks. Creation races yield one complete winner; errors, including post-publication fsync failure, remain observable without pretending rollback.

SW100-C0345.scope: Cooperating local instances reload under flock; serialized metadata mutations/rotation and fresh reads preserve concurrent additions/revocations.
SW100-C0345.rationale: Each local cooperating operation acquires a fresh flock descriptor and reloads persisted metadata under that lock. Complete synced replacement and current reads retain concurrent additions and revocations; rotation is serialized. Stale readers cannot recover a revoked private key even after backend deletion fails, and mismatched keyring/private material is rejected. Metadata/keyring are separate stores, not a joint crash-atomic transaction.

SW100-C0533.scope: Only legitimate absence initiates exclusive creation. Corruption/decryption errors preserve identity and now fail before quote/TSA/output.
SW100-C0533.rationale: The consumer creates an identity only on FileNotFoundError. Invalid JSON and AEAD/wrong-passphrase errors propagate without forging/replacing the seed and now precede quote/TSA/output operations. Real temporary corrupted/wrong-passphrase seeds preserve exact bytes; valid software fixture integration still signs the complete v2 manifest.

limits: All runtime effects confined to synthetic HOME/CORTEX_DB_PATH, copied scripts, real temporary SQLite/WAL and software keys. TCP/DNS and dotenv disabled. No operator identity, ledger actor, hardware, TSA, deployment or Git mutation executed.
Local cooperative POSIX filesystem locking/hard-link/directory-fsync contract only; no isolation from a malicious same-UID writer replacing ancestors or lockfiles.
No physical power-cut test. Abrupt process failure may leave unpublished DB/staging artifacts; no automatic orphan deletion/recovery claim.
A failure after atomic publication can leave complete new identity/metadata visible; failure is explicit, not an atomic rollback guarantee.

Keyring and metadata remain separate stores without a joint crash-atomic transaction; in-memory fallback is not durable secret storage. Revocation blocks current API access, not previously copied private keys.
Snapshot hashes bind content integrity, not authenticated authorship. The sealer hardcoded passphrase and general artifact overwrite policy are outside these five findings.
A concurrent edit sequence was preserved by S1 before user reserved the file. Review approves only the final hashes above.
